sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13.07.2023 at about 11.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HY- 5342, carefully, by following the traffic rules and regulations.

When he reached near Canara Bank, Sharavathi Road, Yelanka New Town, Bengaluru, at that time, a car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715 came from opposite road, driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
so as to endangering human life and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Navachethana Hospital, Yelanka, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.

Earlier to the accident, he was working as Proprietor, Stuffed Roles and Momos, Gaurdamall,
Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.120,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA- 9715.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non- compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it has contended that,
the alleged car is not at all involved in the alleged accident and there is no rash or negligent driving Hemanth R B vs Mananna F Harijan on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87580506/
2 on the part of the driver of the said car and the petitioner himself was negligence in causing the accident.

sentences.text: The petitioner in collusion with the respondent No.1 and the jurisdictional Police has filed a false complaint against the driver of insured car, in order to get wrongful gain.

Further it has contended that the driver of the car was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and the car was not having valid permit and fitness certificate, as on the date of accident and the owner of said car has willfully entrusted his vehicle to the person not holding valid driving licence and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Further it has contended that, the alleged accident has taken place on 13.07.2023 and complaint is lodged on 14.07.2023, after lapse of one day from the date of alleged accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 13.08.2023 at about 11.30 p.m., near Canara Bank, Sharavathi Road, Yelahanka New Town, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 25-AA-9715 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?

sentences.text: 3 9. Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 13.07.2023 at about 11.30 p.m., when he was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HY-5342, carefully and by following traffic rules and regulations and reached near Canara Bank, Sharavathi Road, Yelahanka New Town,
Bengaluru, at that time, the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715 came from opposite road, driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as Proprietor at Stuffed Roles and Momos, Gaurdamall, Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of First Information Statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Sketch, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Notice under Sec.133 of M.V.A. Act,
Ex.P.5 is true copy of reply to said notice, Ex.P.6 is true copy of Charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.8 are medical bills, Ex.P.9 is the prescriptions, Ex.P.10 is the notarized copies of Aadhar cards, Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of PAN card, Ex.P.12 is notarised copy of and Driving Licence, Ex.P.13 is notarized copy of M-tech Degree Certificate, Ex.P.14 is true copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.15 is Clinical Note and Ex.P.16 is X- ray.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6 and Ex.P.14,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715, while taking turn towards right side and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HY-5342 of the petitioner, which was proceeding on the left side of the road.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injury on his right leg.

The investigation officer in his final report,
marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 25-AA-9715 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injury on his right leg in the said accident.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-25-AA-9715 and its validity as on the date of accident
, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-25-AA-9715 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the respondent No.1 and jurisdictional Police has filed a false complaint Hemanth R B vs Mananna F Harijan on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87580506/
4 against the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715, in order to get wrongful gain from the respondent No.2 insurance company.

sentences.text: But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any oral evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the above contentions on oath.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and the petitioner in collusion with the respondent No.1 and jurisdictional Police has filed a false complaint against the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-25-AA- 9715, while taking right turn and dashing the same against the motorcycle of the petitioner
. Further it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury on his right leg in the said accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length

,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 40 feet wide Sharavathi road, near Canara Bank, Yalahanka New Town, Bengaluru, in between offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715 and two wheeler bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HY-5342 of the petitioner, who was proceeding on the left side of the said road towards Chikka-bommasandra and the driver of offending vehicle was taking right turn towards 10th A Sector, Yelanaka New Town.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false or concocted documents.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-25-AA-9715 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.14 Wound certificate, Ex.P.7 Discharge summary, Ex.P.14 OPD book, Ex.P.15 Clinical note and Ex.P.16 X-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injury to his right leg in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has suffered right leg both bones fracture.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.

On the other hand,
there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical Hemanth R B vs Mananna F Harijan on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87580506/

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injury in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 13.07.2023 at about 11:30 p.m., near Canara Bank, Sharavathi Road, Yelanka New Town, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715.

Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715 and he has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained fracture both bones of left leg and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copies of his Aadhar card, PAN card and Driving licence, which are marked as Ex.P.10 to 12.
As per Ex.P.10 to 12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 16.05.1994.
The accident has taken place on 13.07.2023 at about 11:30 p.m.

Therefore, the age of the petitioner as Hemanth R B vs Mananna F Harijan on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87580506/
6 on the date of accident was 29 years.

sentences.text: Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right leg both bones fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 42% physical disability of Right lower limb and 14% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.14 wound certificate,
Ex.P.7 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 Clinical note and Ex.P.16 X-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injury and he has undergone surgery for the said injury.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.
But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 13.07.2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 14.07.2023.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture is united with implants in situ and if the range of movements are improved, the disability will be reduced.
Further he has clearly admitted that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability and the petitioner can do desk job.

Therefore, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was a Proprietor of Stuffed Roles and Momos, Garudamall, Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injury suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was a Proprietor of Stuffed Roles and Momos, Garudamall, Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner at Rs.1,92,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 29 years is 17.

ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 8 medical bills, as per Ex.P.8.

All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has wrongly calculated the total amount, actually the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,02,204/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,02,204/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e. fracture of both bones of right leg.
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary

, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days from 14.07.2023 to 16.07.02023, in Navachethana Hospital, Yelahanka,
Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injury has caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore,
taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days in Navachethana Hospital, Yelahanka, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 3 = Rs.3,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days in Navachethana Hospital, Yelahanka, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 3 = Rs.2,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of 5th Cross, Balaji Layout, Phase-2,
Madappanahalli, Singanayakanahalli, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place near Canara Bank,
Sharavathi Road, Yelanka New Town, Bengaluru and the petitioner has taken treatment at Navachethana Hospital, Yelahanka, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 3 days as in-patient at Navachethana Hospital, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore,
Rs.16,000 x 2 = Rs.32,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 29 years and unfortunately he has suffered right leg both bones fracture.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.

sentences.text: Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost around Rs.60,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,26,400-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,02,204-00 3. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00 4. Attendant charges 3,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 2,400-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 32,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,71,004/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA- 9715.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the driver of offending vehicle by name Ramanna Fakirappa Harijana S/o Fakeerappa, was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA- 3120220004690 to drive the said vehicle and it is valid till 31.05.2023 and the offending vehicle was insured by respondent No.2 insurance company vide Policy No.98000031220112234136 and it was valid from 30.10.2022 to 29.10.2023.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 13.07.2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-25-AA- 9715 the said accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Hemanth R B vs Mananna F Harijan on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87580506/
9 vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

sentences.text: Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,71,004/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,71,004/- (Rupees five lakh seventy one thousand and four only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 13.08.2023 at about 11.30 p.m., near Canara Bank, Sharavathi Road, Yelahanka New Town, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 25-AA-9715 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injury in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 13.07.2023 at about 11:30 p.m., near Canara Bank, Sharavathi Road, Yelanka New Town, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injury on his right leg.
The investigation officer in his final report,
marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 25-AA-9715 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injury on his right leg in the said accident.
Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-25-AA-9715 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-25-AA-9715 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Further he has clearly admitted that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability and the petitioner can do desk job.
Therefore, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was a Proprietor of Stuffed Roles and Momos, Garudamall, Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e. fracture of both bones of right leg.
Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the driver of offending vehicle by name Ramanna Fakirappa Harijana S/o Fakeerappa, was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA- 3120220004690 to drive the said vehicle and it is valid till 31.05.2023 and the offending vehicle was insured by respondent No.2 insurance company vide Policy No.98000031220112234136 and it was valid from 30.10.2022 to 29.10.2023.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 13.07.2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-25-AA- 9715 the said accident in question has taken place.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons,
holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,71,004/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,71,004/- (Rupees five lakh seventy one thousand and four only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
